documentedBehavior: Working memory is Postgres, isolated by record schema and role. Browsers read through the head, never directly.
The graph projects the record exactly once per row; readers can see its projection position and how far behind it is.
Ledger adoption moves operational rows to memory; unavailable adopted ledger blocks admission with no fallback to git.
Knowledge binding uses locus subtree paths or exact graph node identities, and Work reads a deduplicated scoped package.
Protected receipts stay sealed in memory. Reads require reader-and-purpose disclosure and an audit row before the body is returned; holds prevent redaction.
proposedReadModels: Memory availability, routing, projection watermark, and observation time summary.
Knowledge table joined with bindings, family, ratification Review, and supersession.
Protected receipt metadata with authorized disclosure and hold state.
Recent operational ledger rows through the generated head surface.
unsupportedActions: Generated RPC handler coverage for these read models is not established by the prose docs.
No direct database access, graph editing, arbitrary receipt read, or unaudited protected-body download is offered.
Receipt actions are metadata inspection only in the wireframe; no disclosure, reading, or redaction is executed.

documentedBehavior: Record is an append-only git journal of decisions, changes, Reviews, practices, grants, connections, and people.
Chain rows retain authorship and are checked against local or signed trust policy.
Candidate pointers and receipt references travel with record sync.

A connection is Board-approved, scoped by purpose and evidence classes, and requires an independent verdict. Explicit handoffs carry provenance; receipt bodies and whole journals do not cross connections.
proposedReadModels: Paged timeline joined with entity labels and relevant evidence.
Record identity, chain verification, remote synchronization and trust summary.
Retained candidates with review status and revision links.
Connections and latest handoff acceptance state.
unsupportedActions: Generated RPC coverage for unified history, candidate provenance and connection queries remains unverified.
Timeline names are presentation labels for documented events; fixture row numbers and identifiers are illustrative.
No rewind, journal edit, candidate deletion, or connection mutation is offered.

documentedBehavior: Genome owns application source, organization source and vendored DNA; it does not hold operational work or secrets.
Source changes become candidates with source and structural diffs and verification evidence.
The compiler rejects unchecked or law-breaking candidates before review; grants and impact determine review authority.
Organization changes and law, effects or ownership hard boundaries require Board review.
Grants are constructor arguments in source, not runtime settings.
Vendor DNA is refreshed by the toolchain upgrade path.
proposedReadModels: Source roots and pinned revision/provenance summary.
Candidate summary joined to verification receipts, semantic/source differences and required authority.
Human-readable grant and constitutional-claim summary from checked organization source.
unsupportedActions: Generated RPC read and command coverage for genome browsing, candidate comparisons and Review decisions remains unverified.
Candidate diff is a narrative fixture summary; actual structural diff schema is not assumed.
No inline source editing, runtime grant widening, one-click direct apply or raw vendored-core editing is offered.
Review requirements explain the documented workflow but do not submit a verdict in this prototype.

documentedBehavior: Ask, claim, settle and read are the spine's operations; asks and refusals are recorded.
Definitions bind in full by revision before admission. Every step names exactly one write-store. A step completes after all registered members settle.
Execution, step, work and attempt identities survive restart. Outcomes already recorded do not run again.
Human leaves become cases on the Board queue. Uncertain prior effects wait for human resolution.
Schedules name a definition, cadence, convener and inputs. Misses and skips are recorded; missed occurrences do not catch up.
Schedule pause/resume and declaration requests are documented CLI flows; generated surface exposure has not been verified.
proposedReadModels: Execution list joined with current step, performer, authority and durable state
Workflow catalog with admission refusal reasons and input schema
Schedule listing with occurrence counts and latest execution
Generated @rpc contract names and authorization for these read models require integration verification.
unsupportedActions: No root cancellation button: cancellation is an internal engine message with no documented CLI sender.
No direct workflow deploy, vault rotation, or host provisioning actions: corresponding baseline definitions are currently refused at admission.
Wireframe opens flow previews only; it does not issue schedule or execution commands.
spine.fixtures: All execution IDs, names, status counts and schedules shown are invented sample data. close-month is adapted from the documentation example.

documentedBehavior: Work verbs claim, brief, renew, allowance, submit, settle and release act under the current position and lease.
The person must hold the claimed position under OIDC/normal graph authority; local-trust fallback is distinct.
Submit and release are idempotent under the attempt/token request identity. The owner settles the outcome separately.
An uncertain performer with unresolved effect is not automatically retried; its worker slot stops and a person resolves ok or failed.
A worker loop supervises separate holders. Human work or unavailable model capability can hand work to a person.
proposedReadModels: Attempt list with performer, effect class, lease metadata and settlement state
Worker loop/slot projection linked to durable attempts
Human resolution history with evidence
Generated browser-accessible command bindings and allowed-action projection require verification; documented work transport includes local socket commands.
unsupportedActions: No automatic retry or resolve button for uncertain external effects.
No UI operation claiming a position merely because its name exists.
No loop drain button, since a local CLI marker is not a verified remote browser operation.
Claim and outcome interactions are previews, not submitted commands.
legs.fixtures: All attempts, worker slots, evidence and outcomes are illustrative.

documentedBehavior: Hands expose git in a scratch clone, forge Review creation/verdict reads, toolchain checks, and lease/allowance operations.
A Patch Work returns commit:<sha> and its patch receipt. The owner applies and verifies it and opens Review.
A leg never merges. Deploy and heart are explicitly refused hands today.
proposedReadModels: Work-specific tool grant and available interface matrix
Patch receipt and verification trail linked to a Work
Generated inspection bindings and authority for receipt visibility require verification.
unsupportedActions: No deployment, heart control, forge merge or broad credential access.
No global editable tool grant inferred from the interface inventory.
hands.fixtures: The scratch commit and changed-file count are illustrative.

documentedBehavior: Hat is structured per-Work context including position, charter, ratified practices, objective, target, output, data/effect classes, budget, grant, knowledge, history and snapshot identity.
On an OIDC head only the person who claimed and still holds the attempt lease may read its hat. Otherwise lease_required is returned.
Hat identity includes record head, memory watermark and digest. Rendering is performer-local text, prompt or agent; renderer and rendering digests return with the outcome.
proposedReadModels: Current user's claimed Work context, never an unrestricted organism-wide context browser
Rendered brief and snapshot identity inspector
Existing documented /dna/context semantics must be preserved by the eventual generated @rpc binding.
unsupportedActions: No account/admin bypass to browse hats belonging to other active lease holders.
No in-place edit of immutable context snapshot or arbitrary prompt injection field.
No broad environment or credential viewer.
hat.fixtures: The current claim, charter, practice, grant, digests and evidence bindings are sample values. Riley holds position:agent and is the person mapped to the current claim through worker holder position:agent#1.

documentedBehavior: Source-owned leader/editor/agent routers select quick, deep and private backends.
Hosted model credentials name vault slots; secret bytes are never returned. Missing credential slots refuse before the wire.

The model-call budget accounts model.called rows. Its per-attempt allowance is min(Work ceiling, remaining window), not a reservation; concurrent attempt allowances can overrun a window. This is distinct from money delegated under an autonomy Grant: shaping.md documents grant.reserved before that money effect, and dna.md describes money reserved and settled against a grant.
Calls include adapter, backend, model, tokens, cost and time as evidence. Budget exhaustion refuses model-backed work; Board decisions need no model.
RecordedModel captures answers by complete request identity and harness patches. Keyless replay refuses misses; it does not measure model quality.
proposedReadModels: Budget and per-position spend projection over model.called
Redacted model catalog and allowed routing summary
Call/tape metadata inspector without secret bytes or unrestricted prompt bodies
Generated API catalog, budget and tape visibility remain to be verified.
unsupportedActions: No secret/key editing or revealing secret bytes.
No live model probing button: documented probe spends outside the organism's journal and needs a deliberate future flow.
No live route editor or replay execution button inferred from source-defined configuration.
voice.fixtures: Budget totals, call counts, route choices, costs and tape entries are invented examples, not runtime telemetry or product pricing.

documentedBehavior: An attached application has its own data, secrets and API, and a publish-only account on its own application subjects.
Application events are recorded as reading.recorded before action and acknowledged after landing or permanent refusal; duplicate entities are refused.
concern.raised events can become concern.requested; generic readings are retained without automatic action.
Application expression follows an exact reviewed candidate, with deployment/restart receipts, an observation window and retention or rollback.
application remove records detachment and revokes the application's broker account.
proposedReadModels: Application summary with purpose, seed, attachment state, API boundary and subject scope.
Joined expression history from Mutation, Review, fleet, instance and observation rows.
Recent recorded application readings with payload details.
Generated @rpc method names, transport mapping, authority and streaming endpoints for these models remain unverified.
unsupportedActions: A multi-application or foreign-language Heart management UI is not established by the inspected current heart.md.
Performer HeartHand and DeployHand are NoHeart/NoDeploy; workflows that write the heart are refused at admission.
No real application mutation, deployment, detachment or network request is implemented by this prototype.

documentedBehavior: One body per record, or per owner on shared records, holds a renewing lease; a body that loses it stops.
body claim --force and body release [--force] record lease operations.
Body provisioning/start/stop/logs are documented operator CLI operations.
Fleet nodes report instance.up and instance.exited; deployment requests carry revision, plan, seed, affected instances and reason.
Reviewed fleet expression waits up to three minutes for every touched instance, then an observation window; failure triggers a rollback deployment of the same affected instances.
Manual deploy and rollback CLI operations are documented.
proposedReadModels: Lease snapshot, current holder and latest tick/expiry.
Fleet instance table joined from plan and latest instance receipt.
Deployment and rollback traces connecting requests, per-instance receipts and Mutation outcomes.
Generated @rpc read/action mappings and operator permissions are unverified; preview controls correspond only to documented CLI semantics.
unsupportedActions: No claim that a deployment request means completion; instance evidence remains separate.
No generalized capacity/autoscaling, rolling-deploy policy designer or arbitrary host orchestration was inferred.
Lease release and deploy are local previews only; no action executes.

documentedBehavior: NATS JetStream carries signals under organization scopes; one disk stream retains one week.
The spine durable reads DNA facts; the heart durable lands application events; head.row.landed prompts Face refresh.
Unanswered request rows relay every 30 seconds; stream acknowledgement does not replace the answering record row.
Delivery is at least once and consumers deduplicate by request/entity IDs.
An undeliverable connection records a violation, releases the body lease and exits with restart code 75; the supervisor restarts it.
proposedReadModels: Subject-route and role visibility.
Pending asks computed by request IDs and answering kinds.
Record-grounded delivery failures and request traces.
Publish-acknowledgement stage in the sample trace may require transport observability beyond durable record rows; generated API support remains unverified.
unsupportedActions: No direct browser connection to NATS or credentials.
No manual arbitrary message publication, acknowledge/replay controls or stream deletion in the wireframe.
No assertion that private broker counters or durable-consumer lag are already exposed through @rpc.

documentedBehavior: Prometheus stores one week of part pulse, node instance-up/since and spine model-call readings.
Readings are signals; a part may run unread if its metrics port cannot bind, and store failure does not stop the organism.
Pressure and concerns enter as request rows and are relayed until answered.
Three answered pressure raises at one source propose an appendage; initiative may create an organization Mutation but the Board decides.
Concerns route a locus path to its parent; three occurrences can propose parent-bound knowledge for Board review.
proposedReadModels: Telemetry summary per part/node/instance with explicit timestamps.
Pressure and concern summaries joined to request, answer, proposal and Review rows.
Authority-aware raise-pressure admission API and concern detail routing remain to be mapped.
Metrics are on a private services tier; an authorized aggregate @rpc surface for Face consumption is unverified.
unsupportedActions: No automatic telemetry-to-pressure derivation beyond documented reflex concern behavior.
No per-task, per-event or per-revision Prometheus series; tasks join spend and receipts through rows.
Raise-pressure action is a bounded local preview only; no receipt is fabricated.

documentedBehavior: Only instance.down is built in, checking dna_instance_up=0 every five seconds by default.
One firing per outage publishes reflex.fired; the heart lands a reading before the named node acts.
The node restarts only that instance at the latest deployment revision and writes reflex.acted with restarted, already up or failure reason.
A second firing for a target within ten minutes becomes a concern once per window; a failed restart also becomes a concern.
A store failure means no readings to fire on. The current local Face start script starts and stops reflexes.
proposedReadModels: Read-only rule summary from actual deployed configuration.
Firing trace joining reading.recorded, reflex.acted and concern.requested.
Generated @rpc list/detail endpoints, permissions and remote Habitat reflex process management are unverified.
unsupportedActions: No custom rule creation, threshold editor or arbitrary action declaration exists in the inspected docs.
No automatic backoff or rollback is attributed to reflexes; observation rollback belongs to expression delivery.
No enable/disable, retry, force-fire or restart action is exposed by this wireframe.
